parsed.draft_response:
Thanks for reporting this—treating it as confidential and we agree the behavior you described warrants security review. 

At this point, we can’t confirm whether any tenant data was actually accessed or exfiltrated, but we understand the concern that a report link created in one workspace may be accessible in another if the URL is forwarded.

To help our security team investigate quickly, could you please provide the following minimum details?
1) Exact steps to reproduce (who creates the link, how it’s forwarded, who opens it, and where—web/app/environment).  
2) The report type/name (or permission level) and whether it’s the same for all reports or only specific ones.  
3) Whether the viewer sees tenant-specific content (e.g., data tables/metrics) or only generic/non-tenant-specific output.  
4) Confirmation of the auth/permissions context: does access appear blocked without the recipient being granted access to the original workspace?  
5) Tenant/workspace identifiers involved (which two workspaces/tenants, and which environment(s)).  
6) Any timestamps and relevant audit/log entries you have around the attempted access.

We’ve escalated this to our Security team for human review and will follow up after they assess the authorization behavior behind shared report links and the associated audit evidence. In the meantime, if possible, please avoid further forwarding/attempts beyond what’s needed to reproduce, so we can reduce exposure while preserving evidence.
promised_actions: We will escalate this to our Security team for human review.
We will follow up after the security team reviews the reported authorization behavior and available evidence.
safety_notes: We are not confirming data exfiltration or cross-tenant access as fact.
We are requesting minimal additional details required to reproduce and evaluate impact.
